an4.42:1.3: “Categorical” (“one-sided”, _ekaṁsa_) statements include Devadatta’s rebirth ([an6.62:4.2]()); the things that don’t lead to dispassion are not Dhamma ([an7.83:2.4]()); and the Buddha’s imminent passing ([dn16:3.48.4]()). The Jains have a philosophy of _anekaṁsavāda_ according to which all statements can bvee seen from multiple different perspectives.
an4.42:1.4: Questions “needing analysis” (_vibhajja_) include whether all forms of mortification should be condemned ([an10.94:4.4]()); whether laypeople or renunciates succeed in the Dhamma ([mn99:4.4]()); and Potaliputta’s questions about kamma and feeling ([mn136:5.3]()).
an4.42:1.5: Questions requiring a “counter-question” (_paṭipucchā_) include who sleeps well in the world ([an3.35:3.1]()); whether reunciate life is more virtuous than sacrifice ([an3.60:2.1]()); and who has a good teaching and practice ([an3.72:2.4]()).
an4.42:4.1: Comm: Durāsado duppasahoti parehi ghaṭṭetuṁ vā abhibhavituṁ vā na sakkā
